as_told.title: AARO under Kirkpatrick acted as counterintelligence and a honey trap, harassing whistleblowers

plain: A writer on national security, Matthew Pines, says that once US government work on unexplained sightings moved into AARO, a Pentagon office set up to look into such reports, it was compromised by people from the CIA, the US spy agency, and from the Air Force, such as Sean Kirkpatrick, who ran the office. A filmmaker and journalist, Jeremy Corbell, goes further. He says AARO worked as counterintelligence against the American public, acting like a honey trap that drew in whistleblowers and then harassed them, and he credits sources including the journalist George Knapp. If true, it would mean the office meant to find answers was built to hide them.
